To convert the measure of an angle in radians to an equivalent measure in degrees, we multiply the measure in radians by [MATH: \dfrac{180^\circ}{\pi}.] This gives

[MATH: \left(-\dfrac{2\pi} 3 \right) \cdot \left(\dfrac {180^\circ} {\pi}\right) = -120^\circ.]

Therefore, [MATH: -\dfrac{2\pi}{3}] is equivalent to [MATH: -120^\circ.]

  • A positive angle has a rotation that is measured counter-clockwise, and a negative angle is measured clockwise.

Therefore, the correct diagram is as follows:
